title: Developer Behind the AI-Built Adobe Clones Says They Are “Not Anywhere Close to Ready
gist: Brandon Thomas's AI-built (Claude Opus 5.5, Rust) open-source Adobe clone suite PhotoCraft has ~76% feature breadth but only ~45% readiness for real work, 579 open issues and PSD interchange failures, after 2,152 commits in 14 days; the developer says he was not ready to post it, and commenters dispute the clean-room claim and the one-month parity timeline.

insights.claim: Brandon Thomas built AI-generated open-source replacements for seven Adobe applications in Rust with WebAssembly builds using Claude Opus 5.5, licensed MIT and Apache.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Shows a single developer with agents can generate suite-scale software clones in weeks.
insights.locator: Thomas used Claude Opus 5.5 to build the applications in Rust

insights.claim: In its first 14 days PhotoCraft's repository logged 2,152 commits, 1,004 merged pull requests and 539,017 lines of Rust across 1,306 files, with 317 contributor identities and Claude named as commit author 277 times.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Agentic code-generation throughput is extreme, but contributor count contradicts the 'solo developer' narrative.

insights.claim: PhotoCraft's roadmap puts feature breadth near 76% but readiness for real work about 45% (43% for mainstream practitioners, 61% for core-feature users), showing that feature counts overstate usability.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Parity claims based on feature counts are misleading; readiness metrics matter for adoption.

insights.claim: The roadmap estimates beta is 1,100 to 1,800 hours away and full parity 2,300 to 4,100 hours, counted as Opus 5.5 agent wall-clock hours for one agent working sequentially, against Photoshop 2026 version 27.11.0.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Agent-hours is a new unit of effort estimation for AI-built software.

insights.claim: The roadmap reports 579 open issues, 22 of 25 missed performance budgets and that 'PSDs we write are not yet reliably accepted by Photoshop', which undermines it as a replacement because file interchange is core.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: File-format compatibility is the key moat for incumbents like Adobe.
insights.quote: PSDs we write are not yet reliably accepted by Photoshop.
insights.locator: The roadmap’s own account of why the project is still alpha

insights.claim: Thomas posted to Hacker News saying the project was not ready, while earlier posts across five subreddits projected beta and roughly 100% parity within a month; he later said 99% parity would be 'measured in months and not years'.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Hype-driven timelines for AI-built software tend to be walked back quickly.
insights.quote: 99% parity will take a while, but I’m sure it’ll be measured in months and not years.
insights.locator: Brandon Thomas put his AI-built open-source replacements

insights.claim: Users reported the Photoshop clone lacks basics such as alt-eyedropper and flexible layouts, photographers hit RAW noise, banding and missing support for several Nikon bodies, while the simplest app, PDFCraft, worked without bugs.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: AI-built clones work for simple tools but fail on complex professional workflows.
insights.locator: People who installed the apps split along a line

insights.claim: Commenter az_liberal_geek, building the Hew SketchUp replacement with Claude, said a fast first version looked great but was buggy, with each major feature needing hours of Claude development plus many hours of human testing, and put parity at a year, not a month.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: The last 20% of polish still demands heavy human effort, limiting disruption of incumbents.
insights.locator: The most measured voice came from someone running the same experiment

insights.claim: PhotoCraft's AGENTS.md states a clean-room rule, studying Adobe editors for behaviour and look only and implementing from public specs, but commenter kmeisthax argued there is no such thing as clean-room vibe coding because the doctrine assumes separated teams.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: IP and legal risk around AI-generated clones of proprietary software is unresolved.
insights.quote: There is no such thing as clean-room vibe coding.
insights.locator: That language is where opinion divides.

insights.claim: The repository gates every change with tests, a panic_hunt test fuzzing commands with adversarial parameters, checks against a corpus of Photoshop-authored PSDs, and a JSON control channel plus MCP server so the coding agent can drive and screenshot the running app.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Agent-driven verification loops are what make large-scale AI code generation feasible.
insights.locator: Little of the coverage mentioned how much process sits in the repository
